metaDesc: Where to go for cool air and a sea of mist in Thailand’s cool season? Six picks — Pai, Nan, Mae Hong Son, Chiang Khan, Khao Kho and Chiang Rai — with where to stay.

blocks.html: Short answer: In the north choose Pai (easy mist and views), Mae Hong Son (Pang Ung) or Nan (Doi Phu Kha/Pua); in the upper Isan, Chiang Khan (Loei) on the Mekong; and for the sea of mist closest to Bangkok, Khao Kho (Phetchabun).

items.name: Pai (Mae Hong Son)
items.blurb: A small town in a valley — cool air, easy-to-see mist, laid-back cafés and a night walking street, perfect for a first mountain trip.

items.name: Mae Hong Son
items.blurb: A misty valley town — Pang Ung and Ban Rak Thai offer dawn mist over the lake, and it anchors the 1,864-curve loop drive.

items.name: Nan
items.blurb: A quiet old town plus mountains — head to Pua and Doi Phu Kha for terraced fields, mist and scenic mountain cafés.

items.name: Chiang Khan (Loei)
items.blurb: A Mekong town of old wooden houses — cool air, dawn sticky-rice alms and mist at Phu Thok; it is busy in winter, so book ahead.

items.name: Khao Kho (Phetchabun)
items.blurb: The “Switzerland of Thailand” — the sea of mist closest to Bangkok, with many hill-view resorts and an easy drive, great for a weekend.

items.name: Chiang Rai
items.blurb: The far north — cool air, tea plantations, Doi Tung and Doi Chang, beautiful temples and the mist at Phu Chi Fa, good for several days.

faq.q: Where is coldest in Thailand’s cool season?
faq.a: High summits like Phu Thap Boek (Phetchabun), Doi Inthanon (Chiang Mai) and the high peaks of Chiang Rai/Mae Hong Son are coldest, sometimes near 0°C; the deepest cold is Dec–Jan, so pack warm layers.

faq.q: When should I go to see the sea of mist?
faq.a: Nov–Feb has the thickest mist and coolest air; head to the viewpoint before sunrise. Long weekends are crowded and rooms sell out fast, so book ahead.

faq.q: Can I visit the mountains without a car?
faq.a: Pai and Chiang Khan are easy without a car — the towns are walkable with rentals and tours — while the outskirts of Nan, Khao Kho and Mae Hong Son really need a car or motorbike, as the sights are spread out.
